Frequently Asked Questions.

Complex questions? You’re speaking our language.

BigCommerce is an open ecommerce platform that helps businesses build, manage, and scale online stores. It provides a hosted storefront, secure checkout, payment integrations, and multichannel selling tools without requiring businesses to maintain their own infrastructure.

BigCommerce includes unlimited products, multi-storefront management, native B2B capabilities, omnichannel integrations, SEO tools, and support for headless and composable commerce through Catalyst. Businesses can also extend functionality through 1,200+ apps and integrations available in the BigCommerce ecosystem.

BigCommerce offers plans for businesses of all sizes, from growing brands to enterprise organizations. Current pricing and plan details are available at https://www.bigcommerce.com/pricing/﻿

BigCommerce does not charge payment fees on orders processed through eligible Embedded Payment Providers. Standard payment processing fees from your chosen payment provider still apply.

﻿

If you use a non-embedded payment provider, additional transaction fees could apply depending on your plan. Contact our team for details on supported payment providers and pricing.

BigCommerce offers more built-in functionality, including native B2B capabilities, product filtering, multi-storefront support, and payment freedom without added fees. Shopify is often considered easier for beginners, while BigCommerce is frequently chosen by growing, mid-market, and enterprise businesses with more complex requirements. You can compare each platform here.

﻿BigCommerce B2B Edition includes a broad set of B2B capabilities out of the box, including quote-to-cart workflows, bulk ordering tools, purchase order support, net payment terms, requisition lists, approval workflows, company account hierarchies, and a dedicated Buyer Portal. Many of these capabilities are available natively through B2B Edition rather than requiring a separate app.

﻿

Shopify Plus B2B covers many core B2B requirements and benefits from a large app ecosystem and unified B2B and direct-to-consumer selling. However, businesses with more complex B2B requirements may require additional applications, customization, or development work. BigCommerce B2B Edition also typically starts at a lower price point than Shopify Plus and does not charge additional transaction fees when using Embedded Payment Providers. See pricing for more details.

Yes. BigCommerce includes customizable URLs, meta titles and descriptions, automatic sitemaps, structured data, automated redirects, and other SEO-friendly features designed to improve discoverability.

﻿Migrating to BigCommerce typically involves four steps:

﻿

  1. Auditing your current store data (products, customers, orders, content).
  2. Transferring that data using BigCommerce's import tools or a migration partner.
  3. Rebuilding or redesigning your storefront and configuring integrations.
  4. Launching with 301 redirects in place to help preserve SEO performance.

﻿

BigCommerce provides migration services, implementation support, and a network of certified agency partners that can assist with the entire replatforming process: from data migration and storefront development to integration setup and post-launch testing. Migration timelines vary based on complexity, but many projects are completed in a matter of weeks, while larger enterprise implementations may take several months.

BigCommerce is built to serve businesses at every stage: from small businesses under $5M in online revenue to enterprises earning hundreds of millions.

﻿

Small and mid-size businesses choose BigCommerce for its strong native feature set, payment freedom, and the ability to grow without replatforming.

﻿

Enterprises rely on it for multi-storefront management, headless flexibility, B2B capabilities, and deep ERP integrations. Unlike some platforms that lock advanced features behind expensive tiers, BigCommerce includes a wide range of capabilities on standard plans, making it a strong choice whether you're launching or scaling.

﻿Catalyst is BigCommerce's composable storefront framework built on Next.js and React. It includes Makeswift visual editing, pre-built components, and deep integration with BigCommerce APIs.

Yes. BigCommerce offers native B2B capabilities including customer-specific pricing, quote management, purchase order support, net payment terms, buyer account management, and multi-storefront support.

Yes. Businesses can manage both B2B and B2C experiences from a single platform while supporting different customer types, pricing structures, and storefronts.

﻿Feedonomics is a product feed management platform that optimizes and distributes product data across ad channels, marketplaces, and shopping destinations.

﻿Feedonomics Surface is a self-serve feed management solution available within BigCommerce Channel Manager that helps businesses distribute and optimize product data across major ad channels.

BigCommerce customers can activate Feedonomics Surface directly through Channel Manager. Product data syncs automatically and updates continuously.

Yes. Feedonomics can optimize titles, descriptions, categories, and attributes specifically for Google Shopping without changing how products appear on your storefront.

Yes. Feedonomics supports enterprise-scale catalogs with millions of SKUs and can aggregate product data from multiple sources.

﻿Makeswift is a visual editing platform for Next.js that allows marketers and designers to manage storefront content visually while developers maintain full control over components and code.

﻿Makeswift powers the visual editing experience within BigCommerce Catalyst, allowing teams to build pages, update content, and publish changes without developer involvement for routine updates.

No. Makeswift is designed for non-technical users and provides a visual drag-and-drop editing experience.

Yes. Makeswift helps marketers, designers, and developers collaborate more efficiently while managing storefront content and shared components.

No. Makeswift works with Next.js websites beyond BigCommerce, although it is deeply integrated with BigCommerce Catalyst.﻿
